summary.headline: H1 FY27 revenue fell 57% YoY to ₹39.5 crore as Meta Infotech exited low-margin product sales, while EBITDA margin rose to 8.7% and PAT to ₹4.9 crore.
summary.overview: Management described H1 FY27 as a transition quarter toward a services-led model, with product revenue deliberately cut, mainly from one large banking client. Revenue from operations was ₹39.5 crore versus ₹91 crore in H1 FY26 (stated as "210 crore" in the transcript, which appears to be a transcription error), and rose sequentially from ₹59.9 crore in H2 FY26. EBITDA was ₹7.8 crore (margin 8.7% vs 7.5%), and PAT was ₹4.9 crore versus ₹10.4 crore a year earlier. Management said the investment phase (new vendors, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi, Gulf operations) is complete and that revenue conversion is the next step. The order book was ₹92.7 crore as of September 30.

segments.name: Services (managed / recurring)
segments.commentary: Management says recurring managed services from 30+ customers are the core focus, growing about 8-10% YoY, with a target of adding about ₹7 crore of managed-service revenue each year. Stated H1 managed security revenue was about ₹4 crore, though the transcript is unclear on this figure.

segments.name: Product sales
segments.commentary: Product revenue has been deliberately reduced, mainly from one bank with low margins. Product contracts run 3-5 years and remain a recurring component.

segments.name: Professional services
segments.commentary: One-time implementation work. Management said this business restarts from zero each year and targets ₹5-10 crore of new business per cycle.

guidance_outlook: Management targets recurring profit of about 50% of cost in the near term, rising to 75% and then 100% over the next two to three years (transcript phrasing is unclear).

Management says the long-term target is a 4x growth path from the ₹29 crore base, with growth rates expected to rise each year. Management also cited 13%+ growth expectations, though these figures are hard to confirm from the transcript.
Management says its focus is on profit and gross profit rather than top-line revenue, and expects the next phase of revenue to come from new vendors and locations.
Management said the next few years will see the end of the negative phase and a positive trend, but gave no specific revenue or margin guidance.
capex_capacity: Vendor base grew to about 10 from 2 pre-IPO, with 3 new cybersecurity vendors onboarded in H1 FY27 and more in the pipeline.
Locations expanded from Mumbai alone to Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi and international markets including the Gulf and Nairobi.
Management is targeting 15 top clients each in Mumbai, Bangalore, Hyderabad and Delhi, for 50 accounts in total.
Discussions are underway with one of the largest US business integrators for services-only engagements.
demand_pricing: 12 new clients added in H1 FY27 across sectors and geographies.
Management said AI adoption increases demand for cybersecurity. AI security is at an early stage, and the company is working on a few deals.
Management said it competes on specialisation in niche cybersecurity and claimed that large players are losing share in several accounts. These claims are not independently verified.
Management said the company is not pursuing security consulting, which it views as one-time work with many competitors.

qa_highlights.question: What are the key growth drivers for the next two to three years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company moved away from product revenue after the IPO, added about 8 vendors and new locations, and is now focused on recurring services. It expects the recurring base to grow by about 8-10% YoY, with a long-term target of 4x growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company expanding into new cybersecurity segments or specialised offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will stay in niche product-based cybersecurity with new vendors and will not pursue security consulting.

qa_highlights.question: What is the contribution from the top 5 clients?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a top-5 figure. It said one client had been 30-45% of revenue previously and that the strategy is to spread revenue across about 50 accounts.

qa_highlights.question: How are new regions contributing to revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it does not focus on top line. It said services now make up about 40-45% of the business and that recurring revenue is the priority.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company positioned to capitalise on AI-related cybersecurity demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said AI increases cybersecurity demand and that AI security is an additional offering, with a few deals under discussion but no revenue yet.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue trajectory over the next few quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said investment is complete and that the next phase is converting new vendors and locations into revenue. It did not give a quarterly number.

risks_watch: Revenue fell 57% YoY and the order book of ₹92.7 crore is below historical levels, so revenue conversion is unproven.

Management's disclosures on managed services revenue (about ₹4 crore in H1, ₹7 crore per year additions) and the 'recurring profit' targets are inconsistent or unclear in the transcript; verify with filings.
Dependence on a small set of vendors and on large-client concentration; management declined to disclose top-5 client share.

The transcript's revenue and profit figures contain transcription inconsistencies (for example, H1 FY26 revenue stated as ₹210 crore). Confirm numbers against the filed results before relying on them.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on long-term prospects and the AI-cybersecurity theme, and openly dismissive of near-term top-line weakness. Answers on specifics (client concentration, revenue targets, recurring-profit percentages) were vague or internally inconsistent, and the chairman stressed a long-term view over the stock price.
key_quotes: We consciously decided to continue certain lower margin product sales to a leading bank, one particular bank as part of a strategy to focus on higher value service-equality services.
So after IPO, obviously, statistically we cannot continue with only one location and two vendors. We have added about 10 vendors.
I've always maintained my status as a long-term investment. But definitely in long-term, you will make money.

growth.why: H1 FY27 revenue fell 57% YoY to ₹39.5 crore as low-margin product sales were exited, and management gave no firm revenue guidance, only an aspirational FY29 PAT target of up to 4x FY26 and 8-10% recurring profit growth, backed by vendor additions, new clients and a ₹92.7 crore order book that management itself called below historical levels.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: H1 FY27 EBITDA margin rose to 8.7% from 3.8% in H2 FY26 as low-margin product sales were cut, and management targets rising recurring profit share (50% to 75% to 100% of cost over 2-3 years), though the phrasing is unclear.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Vendors grew to about 10 from 2 and locations now cover Bangalore, Hyderabad, Delhi, Gulf and Nairobi, but these are soft-capacity additions with no capex or capacity figures given and the order book of ₹92.7 crore is below historical levels.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: 12 new clients were added in H1 FY27 and managed services are guided to grow 8-10% YoY, but H1 revenue fell 57% YoY to ₹39.5 crore and no quarterly revenue number was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no revenue or margin guidance and called the order book below historical levels, so an upgrade looks unlikely near term.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Revenue fell 57% YoY and sequential recovery to ₹39.5 crore in H1 is unproven against the FY29 4x PAT aspiration, with management disclosures on recurring revenue and profit targets inconsistent.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: AI-security is an additional offering with a few deals under discussion but no revenue yet, and no product launch date was given.

rows.label: Order book below historical levels
rows.why: The ₹92.7 crore order book at Sep 30 was described by management as below historical levels, which points against a near-term revenue step-up.

rows.label: US business integrator services talks
rows.why: Discussions are underway with one of the largest US business integrators for services-only engagements, but no deal size or timing was disclosed.

rows.label: Shift to services-led model
rows.why: Services rose to about 71% of revenue from about 85% previously, and management says the investment phase is complete and revenue conversion is next, though it gave no quarterly number.

tone.note: Management was confident about the AI-cybersecurity theme, vendor and location expansion and recurring services, but vague on top-5 client share, recurring-profit percentages and revenue targets; analysts pushed on the 57% revenue decline and the order book.
